messages:
paul: Found a surprising UX hole in sampleapps: Rust and .NET samples surface raw HTTP 502/HTML pages as errors, while Node/Python map to ServerError subclasses. New users hit this and file bugs.

anya: Ugh. Do we have a canonical error envelope for the service?

paul: Not fully. We have a proposed envelope in the SDK spec but the edge-case handling (proxies, gzipped bodies, HTML error pages) isn't documented and SDKs parse inconsistently. Example desired envelope: `{"error":{"message":"Quota exceeded","code":"rate_limit","retry_after_ms":1200,"retryable":true,"meta":{"request_id":"r-abc"}}}`.

reza: We need two pieces: 1) server will emit envelope for new responses; 2) SDKs implement a robust normalizer that handles legacy JSON, plaintext, HTML, gzipped payloads, and proxy-wrapped bodies. The normalizer should produce typed exceptions: AuthError, PermissionError, NotFoundError, ConflictError, RateLimitError, ServerError, StreamError.

mike: For streaming: when a chunked stream errors, SDKs should expose `StreamError` with `partial_text` and a `cursor` so apps can resume or show partial content. Also include `retryable` + `last_token_index` in meta.

anya: Good. Also call out common proxy behavior: some CDNs return an HTML error page with 502 but include original JSON in a `<pre>` block. Normalizer should attempt to extract JSON heuristically. But document we can't guarantee parsing every proxy-wrapped body; recommend server owners set proper pass-through.

paul: Backwards compatibility: do not change exception types in patch releases. Implement an opt-in flag `normalize_errors=true` in minor releases and flip default at next major. Provide migration doc.

reza: Agreed. Also prefer `retry_after_ms` over seconds for precision. Keep `code` stable (snake_case) and define a small namespace list for codes in the SDK spec (e.g., rate_limit, quota_exceeded, auth_invalid, permission_denied, model_error).

mike: We should also add a small lint in sampleapp CI that runs the sampleapps (Node, Python, Go, Rust, .NET, Ruby) against a fixture server that returns: envelope JSON, legacy JSON, plaintext, gzipped JSON, and proxy-wrapped HTML. CI asserts the normalized exception class and that `error.code` is consistent across languages.

anya: I'll own the CI fixture and docs stub. ETA EOW.

paul: I'll take Rust + .NET normalizers and sampleapp updates. ETA next Wed.

reza: I'll update the SDK error mapping doc and add the canonical code list and examples for catching by class and by `error.code`. I'll also add a short troubleshooting checklist for "proxy HTML", "missing retry_after", and "stream terminal error with partial text". ETA Thu.

dev-bot: Created ticket INFR-2233: "Error-envelope + robust SDK normalizer + multi-language sampleapp parity" assigned to anya,paul,reza. https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INFR-2233

paul: One implementation detail: for .NET/Objective-C interop keep an integer domain code for old clients but add `ApiErrorCode` string in userInfo for the new behavior. Document this in migration notes.

mike: Monitoring note: emit metric `sdk.error.normalized` when normalizer runs and `sdk.error.unparseable` when we can't extract JSON, so we can measure how often proxies break parity.

anya: Good idea. I'll add those metrics to the fixture CI so infra can alert if `unparseable` > 0.1% during rollout.

reza: Also include examples in docs showing how to build retry/backoff using `retry_after_ms` and `retryable`, and show an example of `on_error(err, partial)` handling for streaming UIs.

paul: Thanks. Let's review in SDK sync Friday.

mike: :thumbsup:
